items.new: Stubb was the second mate. He came from Cape Cod, and so, by local custom, was called a Cape-Cod-man. He was happy-go-lucky, neither coward nor hero, meeting dangers as they came with an air of indifference; and in the tightest crisis of the chase he would keep working away, calm and collected, like a journeyman joiner hired by the year. Good-humored, relaxed, and carefree, he ran his whale-boat as if the deadliest encounter were just a dinner party and his crew all invited guests. He was as fussy about arranging his end of the boat comfortably as an old stagecoach driver is about how snug his seat is. When close up to the whale, in the very death-lock of the fight, he handled his merciless lance coolly and casually, the way a whistling tinker handles his hammer. He would hum his old rigadig tunes while side by side with the most furious monster. For this Stubb, long habit had turned the jaws of death into an easy chair. What he thought about death itself, nobody can say. Whether he ever thought about it at all might be a fair question; but if he ever did happen to turn his mind that way after a comfortable dinner, then no doubt, like a good sailor, he took it as a kind of call of the watch to tumble up aloft and get busy there with something he would find out about when he obeyed the order, and not before.
